blocks.text: In verses 17–20, Jesus explicitly rejects abolishing the Law and the Prophets. The repeated pattern that follows—“You have heard … but I say”—addresses murder, adultery, divorce, oaths, retaliation, and enemies as Jesus’ demanding interpretation of righteousness, rather than as a wholesale contrast between Christianity and Judaism. This remains a debated way of describing the passage, but it helps readers hold the opening claim about fulfillment together with the searching instructions that follow.

Jesus’ instruction not to swear at all culminates in a call for plain, truthful speech: “Yes” and “No” should be enough. Readers and communities disagree about whether this forbids every formal oath or instead condemns manipulative swearing. The stated emphasis in the passage is speech whose truthfulness does not depend on elaborate guarantees.

sections.title: Reading Jesus’ sayings about the law
